lessonMappingReview: Real catalog lessons reread: C2-L005 volume flow and continuity, C2-L006 ideal streamline energy, C2-L007 Newtonian stress and developed profiles, C2-L008 Poiseuille with its domain, C2-L009 series and parallel networks. Candidate course, skill, prerequisites and C6 reuse were checked.
limitations: Only the explicitly assigned ideal physical models are verified. Positive parameters alone do not establish real-fluid laminar regime, no-slip behavior or small-hole asymptotics.
Literal signatures bind exactly the prose read; arbitrary future prose is not semantically parsed.
Exact choice grammar is bounded to rational or decimal literals and one pi or integer-radical monomial, plus the exact reviewed unit suffix. Arbitrary expressions and functions are rejected.

Wrong keys, units, sources, equivalent choices and figure scales are rejected after rebinding and test-only token or edition-hash replacement. The plausible false prose case with a correct key is rejected by frozen reading, not claimed as a general language proof checker.
Conceptual judgments remain AI_CONCEPTUAL separately from EXACT_ORACLE. Human approval is NOT_RUN and all material remains DRAFT.

cases.rejectedBy: Independently reviewed physical scale or graph curve changed

primaryBeforeKeys: Sum positive branch flows at common pressure and invert the resulting conductance. Equivalent resistance is below either finite branch; inverse bounds and fixed-pressure branch closure differ from fixed-total-flow control. The resistances are continuous, not integer counts.

propertyAudit.coverage: Declining-head ODE and finite emptying domain; constant-rate volume additivity; annular profile and Poiseuille scalings in generated low-Re states; telescoping series pressure; parallel flow balance and fixed-pressure closure. Separate tests cover strict inverses, nonlinear means, pi cancellation, coupled roots and reading identity.

records.assetReview: Top network has common absolute pressure drop 106−100 = 6 kPa. Branch flow arrows each 60 px at 20 px/(L/s) give 3 and 3; inlet/outlet arrows 120 px give total 6. Blocks are schematic. At common dp = 6 kPa, flow bars use 40 px/(L/s): A widths 120+120 give 6 L/s; B widths 80+40 give 3 L/s at resistances 3 and 6. The closure panel starts specifically from equal branches A: its first 120 px bar is unchanged while the second is removed, total 6 to 3 L/s. All marker definitions, independent arrow paths, XML and full native image read.
records.distractors: 4 adds series resistances; 2 copies one branch. Numerical 1/2 is one branch conductance, not equivalent resistance. Positive parallel equivalent is below both finite branches.
records.manualArithmetic: At equal resistances 2 each, total conductance is 1/2+1/2 = 1 in reciprocal resistance units. Thus R_eq = 1 kPa·s/L, half either branch.
records.physicalAssumptions: Two passive finite positive continuous branch resistances across common-pressure nodes in a horizontal steady incompressible network. No leakage, storage, additional path, machine or junction losses; taps have equal elevation and kinetic contributions. Q_T is the sum of outgoing branch rates. The closure task explicitly fixes positive node pressure, not total flow; branch closure is a separate infinite-resistance limit.

reviewSequence: All 80 original U3-04 prompts 107–111 were read individually from pinned Git before candidate keys, alternatives or solutions. Primary balances and per-ID exact results were saved first. Then every final candidate prompt, option, full solution and formula, hint, feedback, metadata and provenance was read. Five SVG files were read completely in XML and full native images. Exact root package and binding bytes were compared with the final read author commits before literal signatures were frozen.
scope: Independent AI scientific and pedagogical reading of exact drafts, not human approval or publication.

source.reference: Independently sum positive branch volume rates at common pressure. Invert conductance, retain strict inverse bounds and distinguish a closed branch at fixed pressure from fixed-total-flow control.
